meta.subline: 12 JUL 2026 · 14:00 GST · IRGC DECLARES HORMUZ CLOSED · US ROUND-3 STRIKES · TRUMP–MOJTABA THREAT EXCHANGE · MUSCAT CHANNEL LIVE

banner.html: IRGC NAVY HAS DECLARED THE STRAIT CLOSED ‘UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE.’ Third US strike round in five days · GFS Galaxy hit — crew member missing · southern lane at zero AIS intent · Muscat channel live: Oman two-corridor draft, senior US team expected

wire.title: Third round of US strikes in five days — explosions reported in Bandar Abbas (3), Sirik (2) and on Qeshm Island after Trump orders retaliation for the GFS Galaxy attack.
wire.full: CENTCOM said the strikes began 19:15 ET on 11 Jul (03:15 GST) and were ordered directly by Trump, targeting ‘Iran’s ability to attack commercial vessels.’ IRIB reported three blasts in Bandar Abbas and two in Sirik; Mehr reported explosions on Qeshm Island. No casualty figures yet for this round — the 8-9 Jul rounds killed 14 and wounded 78 across five provinces, with 47 still hospitalised per Iran’s government press office.
wire.why: Round 3 settles the 9 Jul scenario question: this is a sustained campaign, not a two-night spike. The stated target framing — ‘ability to attack commercial vessels’ — ties US strikes explicitly to strait access. This is now a naval-access war, no longer a punitive exchange.

wire.src: IRGC Navy stmt · Bloomberg · Times of Israel
wire.title: IRGC Navy declares the Strait of Hormuz CLOSED ‘until further notice’ — and until the end of US ‘interference’ in the region.
wire.full: The declaration came after the IRGC fired on a vessel it said attempted to transit along an ‘unapproved’ route — the first formal closure declaration since the MOU was signed. The US response, via officials quoted by RFE/RL: Iran ‘does not control’ the Strait of Hormuz. Whether the declaration is enforceable is decomposed in VERIFY.
wire.why: Note what Iran actually executed. Not Bab-el-Mandeb, not NPT withdrawal — the closure of its own strait, the one maximal option fully inside its control. The ‘floats maximal, executes calibrated’ pattern held in form, but the calibrated option has now ratcheted up to a formal closure. The declaration is also a legal position: it converts every southern-route transit into a claimed violation.

wire.title: IRGC hits M/V GFS Galaxy, Cyprus-flagged container ship, 9nm east of Oman — one crew member missing, engine-room fire, vessel disabled.
wire.full: CENTCOM: Iranian forces ‘blatantly attacked’ the GFS Galaxy transiting the strait; a civilian crew member is missing and the vessel cannot continue due to fire and significant engine-room damage. Iran’s account directly contradicts the framing: the IRGC Navy says it fired a ‘warning shot’ at a vessel on an ‘unapproved route.’ Both accounts agree on the operative fact — the ship was on the southern route, without an Iranian permit.
wire.why: The entire route war in one incident: Iran calls southern-route transit a violation; the US calls firing on it an attack. A possible crew fatality would be the first commercial mariner killed since the MOU — a threshold with its own escalation logic. Framing dispute decomposed in VERIFY.

wire.title: Trump and Mojtaba Khamenei trade direct threats — ‘1000 missiles locked and loaded’ vs a vow that avenging his father ‘must certainly be carried out.’
wire.full: Trump warned that ‘1000 Missiles are Locked and Loaded and aimed at the Islamic Republic of Iran’ if Tehran acts on threats to assassinate him, adding the US would ‘completely decimate and destroy all areas of Iran.’ Mojtaba Khamenei answered that revenge for his father’s death ‘is the will of our nation and must certainly be carried out.’ The exchange follows open calls for Trump’s killing at Ali Khamenei’s funeral (4-6 Jul).
wire.why: First direct, personal Trump–Mojtaba exchange of the war. The assassination-revenge axis is a separate escalation channel from the strait dispute — it does not de-escalate when shipping does, and it is the channel Mojtaba personally owns. Per the standing rule, read Trump’s maximal rhetoric against his simultaneous dispatch of negotiators (next item).

wire.title: Muscat channel goes live — Araghchi meets Omani FM; Oman circulates a two-corridor draft; Vance, Rubio, Witkoff and Kushner expected in Muscat.
wire.full: Araghchi met Omani FM Sayyid Badr Albusaidi in Muscat on Saturday; both agreed to further technical and political talks on safe passage. Oman’s draft: two separately controlled corridors, both open — the southern corridor through Omani waters under free pre-war navigation, the northern through Iranian waters requiring prior Iranian approval but with NO tolls. Both sides expressed a desire to return to MOU conditions, but there is no agreement on the wording of Article 5 (transit administration). A senior US team — VP Vance, Sec. Rubio, Witkoff, Kushner — is expected in Muscat.
wire.why: The most senior US delegation of the war, dispatched within hours of Trump declaring the deal dead — the deadline-extension cycle operating in plain view. The Oman draft is the first written formula that gives Iran its permit regime while killing tolls, which is the exact Trump red line. Article 5 wording is now the entire war compressed into one clause.

wire.src: Ynet · Times of Israel · Fox — Israeli officials; no T2 confirmation
wire.title: Israeli leadership signals readiness to rejoin strikes on Iran — officials call the moment ‘more serious than any other time in the past.’
wire.full: Ynet, quoting Israeli officials: Israel is poised to strike Iran, with preparations described as more serious than at any prior point. Times of Israel: Israel is preparing for a renewal of the war if US-Iran negotiations fail, while Trump says Tehran has ‘days’ to make a deal. Israel has not been a party to the MOU and never accepted the Lebanon withdrawal linkage.
wire.why: Labelled PENDING deliberately: all sourcing is Israeli-official via Israeli outlets — no T2 confirmation, and ‘officials say’ leaks are also a pressure instrument in the negotiation. If a T2 source confirms force movements, this becomes the single most consequential item on the board: Israeli re-entry is the one event that makes the MOU unrecoverable.

wire.title: Southern lane at zero — open-source AIS review finds no commercial vessel broadcasting intent to transit the southern shipping lane; IMO advises avoiding the strait.
wire.full: A CBS News review of open-source maritime tracking data on Friday found zero commercial vessels publicly broadcasting locations indicating intent to transit the southern lane. Kpler had recorded 108 transits over 3-5 Jul (a 30-60/day ‘new normal’ range vs ~138/day pre-war per JMIC) before traffic collapsed following the 7-8 Jul vessel attacks. The IMO formally advised ships to avoid the waterway until crew safety can be assured.
wire.why: The de facto closure preceded the de jure one: commercial traffic had already stopped a full day before the IRGC declaration. Iran declared closed a strait that shipping had already abandoned — which is why the declaration was cheap for Tehran to make and why reopening confidence, not the declaration itself, is the metric to watch.

wire.title: Brent closes ~$75.5, +4.7% on the week — Polymarket prices just 4.5% on Hormuz traffic normalising by 31 Jul ($13.8M matched).
wire.full: Brent slipped to ~$75.5 into Friday’s close but held a ~4.7% weekly gain on the renewed disruption (it had traded below $70 on 1 Jul). Polymarket’s normalisation-by-31-Jul market fell from 8.5% to 4.5% across the week. Lloyd’s Market Association: hull war-risk premiums around 5% of vessel value are the emerging market norm for Hormuz transits; softening after the MOU reversed after this week’s attacks. Goldman: Brent above $100 through 2026 if closure runs another month.
wire.why: The market read is calm-ish price, catastrophic probability: a 4.7% weekly move is small against a formal closure because traders assume the closure is a negotiating posture. The 4.5% normalisation odds are the honest number — the market believes the strait stays abnormal through July regardless of what Muscat produces.

wire.title: US official: Iran has downed ~30 US MQ-9 Reaper drones since the war began — the 7 Jul Bushehr shootdown claim remains unconfirmed individually.
wire.full: A US official told ABC that roughly 30 MQ-9s have been lost to Iranian air defences over the course of the war — corroborating the general credibility of IRGC shootdown claims while leaving the specific 7 Jul Khormoj/Bushehr claim unconfirmed. Independent trackers had put cumulative losses between 11 and 24 before this week; treat all totals as a range.
wire.why: Quietly resolves the open VERIFY item from Day 132 at the class level: IRGC drone-kill claims are not propaganda inventions — the loss rate is real and large. It also explains US caution: persistent ISR over Iran is being attrited at ~$30M per airframe.

wire.title: Iran’s regular army joins retaliation — kamikaze drones against a Patriot battery in Kuwait, an early-warning radar in Qatar, and fuel tanks in Bahrain; Jordan also reports intercepts.
wire.full: Iran’s army (Artesh, distinct from the IRGC) said it launched one-way attack drones at named military systems in Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain. Kuwait’s Defence Ministry said it intercepted 3 ballistic missiles, 1 cruise missile and 10 drones, with debris wounding one person. Bahrain reported intercepting ‘several treacherous Iranian aerial attacks.’ Arab News and The National report Jordan among states condemning attacks on its airspace. Saudi Arabia and the GCC issued unified condemnations of Iran — none criticised the preceding US strikes.
wire.why: Two details matter beyond the Day 132 picture: the regular army firing (not just the IRGC) signals institutional breadth behind retaliation, and the target list is precise counter-air-defence work — Patriots and radars — not symbolic fires. Iran is mapping and degrading the GCC intercept architecture while calibrating to zero fatalities.

status.v: DECLARED CLOSED by IRGC Navy ‘until further notice.’ Southern lane at zero AIS intent since Friday; IMO advises avoidance; no confirmed transit on either corridor since the declaration.
Third US strike round in five days (Bandar Abbas, Sirik, Qeshm). Cumulative 8-9 Jul toll: 14 killed, 78 wounded. Israel signalling readiness to rejoin — unconfirmed by any T2 source.

Muscat channel live: Araghchi met Omani FM; Oman two-corridor draft circulating (no tolls, Iranian permits on northern route); Vance, Rubio, Witkoff, Kushner expected. Article 5 wording is the sticking point.
Trump: ‘1000 missiles locked and loaded’ / ‘decimate all areas of Iran.’ Mojtaba: revenge for his father ‘must certainly be carried out.’ Assassination-revenge axis now explicit and personal.

verify.who: Is the Strait of Hormuz actually closed?
verify.quote: The Strait of Hormuz is closed until further notice — until the end of American interference in the region.

rows.c: The declaration was made, and it is Iran’s first formal closure declaration since the MOU.
rows.n: Carried by Iranian state media and confirmed by Bloomberg and Times of Israel reporting of the IRGC Navy statement.

rows.c: Commercial traffic through the southern lane has genuinely collapsed.
rows.n: CBS open-source AIS review found zero vessels broadcasting transit intent on Friday; the IMO has advised avoiding the strait. The collapse preceded the declaration by a day.

rows.c: Whether Iran can enforce closure against opposed traffic.
rows.n: US officials: Iran ‘does not control’ the strait, and US strikes target its anti-ship capability. Against that: the IRGC has demonstrated it can hit unescorted merchants at will (GFS Galaxy, Al Rekayat, Wedyan), which is the only enforcement that matters commercially.
rows.src: US officials via RFE/RL vs demonstrated IRGC strikes

rows.c: Whether northern-route permit holders can still transit ‘closed’ waters.
rows.n: Iran frames the closure as applying to ‘unapproved’ transit — implying its permit regime survives its own closure. No confirmed northern-corridor transit since the declaration to test it.

verify.who: M/V GFS Galaxy — ‘blatant attack’ vs ‘warning shot’
verify.quote: Iranian forces blatantly attacked M/V GFS Galaxy, a Cyprus-flagged container ship transiting the Strait of Hormuz. — CENTCOM

rows.c: The vessel was hit 9nm east of Oman: engine-room fire, significant damage, unable to continue, one civilian crew member missing.
rows.n: CENTCOM statement with vessel-level detail, consistent with maritime-safety reporting; Iran does not deny firing.

rows.c: Intent: deliberate attack on shipping vs ‘warning shot’ at an ‘unapproved route’ transit.
rows.n: Both framings agree on the operative fact — the ship was on the southern route without an Iranian permit. The dispute IS the route war: Iran claims jurisdiction, the US claims freedom of navigation. Do not resolve; render.
rows.src: CENTCOM vs IRGC — irreconcilable by design

rows.c: The fate of the missing crew member.
rows.n: If confirmed dead, this is the first commercial mariner killed since the MOU — a threshold event with its own escalation logic. No recovery or fatality confirmation yet.

verify.quote: Iran has shot down roughly 30 US MQ-9 Reaper drones since the start of the war. — US official, to ABC

rows.c: The claim class is real: MQ-9 losses to Iranian air defences are large-scale and acknowledged inside the US government.
rows.n: A US official putting the figure near 30 validates the pattern of IRGC shootdown claims, resolving the Day 132 open question at the class level.

rows.c: The specific 7 Jul shootdown over Khormoj/Bushehr.
rows.n: Five days on, no CENTCOM confirmation of that individual airframe. Consistent with US practice of not confirming losses individually.

rows.c: Cumulative totals vary wildly by counter: 11, 17, 24, ~30.
rows.n: Independent trackers ran 11-24 before this week; the US official says ~30. Treat every total as a range, never a point estimate.

Hull war-risk ~5% of vessel value is the new norm (LMA). Goldman: Brent >$100 through 2026 if closure runs another month. Weekend markets closed — Monday open prices in the closure declaration.

scenarios.lab: Muscat produces a strikes pause; closure stays declaratory
scenarios.p: The pattern under the noise: both sides escalated kinetically while upgrading their delegations — strikes and talks as parallel tracks. The most senior US team of the war lands in Muscat with a written Omani formula (permits yes, tolls no) that both capitals can sell as victory on Article 5. Iran’s closure declaration becomes the concession it trades away; a pause and a re-drafted Article 5 emerge within 72h. Analytical judgment, not sourced fact.

scenarios.lab: Closure hardens — enforcement fire on any southern transit, round 4
scenarios.p: Article 5 wording stays deadlocked; the IRGC treats the declaration as standing rules of engagement and fires on the first vessel that tests the southern lane. The US answers with round 4 and escort operations, converting the strait into a live US-Iran naval engagement zone. No Israeli participation yet. The longer no vessel tests the lane, the longer this scenario can smoulder without resolving.

scenarios.lab: Israel re-enters — the MOU dies in fact, not just in rhetoric
scenarios.p: Israeli readiness signals become an actual strike package — triggered by talks collapse, an Iranian move on the nuclear file (NPT withdrawal floated 8 Jul), or the assassination-revenge axis producing an attempt. Israeli re-entry is the one event no mediator can walk back: it voids the MOU’s premise, forces Iran to fight on two fronts, and takes strait reopening off the table indefinitely. Elevated from background risk because this is the first explicit Israeli re-entry signalling since the MOU.

uae_means: The strait is now formally closed for the first time since the MOU — but for UAE residents the operative facts are steadier than the headline. UAE airspace remains fully open with no new restrictions through three strike rounds (only Kuwait keeps an overflight ban, to 4 Aug); Emirates and Etihad are flying full schedules. The economic exposure runs through shipping, not skies: with the southern lane at zero and war-risk cover at ~5% of hull value, import costs and fuel-price pass-through resume climbing, and ADNOC’s 2027 full-recovery guidance now looks optimistic rather than conservative. Watch three UAE-specific things: (1) any Iranian projectile aimed at UAE territory — Iran has hit Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar and Jordan this round but conspicuously NOT the UAE, the war’s most-targeted state pre-MOU; that omission is deliberate and reversible; (2) WAM/UAE MOD language shifting from condemning attacks on neighbours to invoking UAE self-defence; (3) the Muscat channel — the two-corridor formula is the only path back to normal Gulf logistics. Stock of essentials is unaffected; there is no indicator of panic-buying conditions. Treat this as severe-but-contained, one Israeli strike package away from uncontained.

triggers.t: First vessel to test the southern lane — if it transits unmolested the closure is bluff; if it is fired on, the strait is a combat zone. Either way the ambiguity ends.
The US team actually sits down in Muscat — Vance/Rubio/Witkoff/Kushner arriving and meeting is the single clearest signal the off-ramp is real. Their cancellation is the counter-signal.
Any T2 confirmation of Israeli force movement — the Ynet/ToI readiness reports upgrading from Israeli-official leaks to confirmed preparations converts the tail scenario to base.
Khamenei Telegram on the closure — the only reliable IRGC-intent signal. Mojtaba personally endorsing ‘until further notice’ makes it policy; his silence leaves it an IRGC Navy position.
A confirmed fatality on the GFS Galaxy — first commercial mariner killed post-MOU would force JWC/insurers to war-zone the entire Gulf and harden every Western position overnight.

hist: War began 28 Feb 2026 — Ali Khamenei killed; Mojtaba Khamenei became Supreme Leader. Iran fired 1,800+ projectiles at the UAE alone (13 killed, 224 injured; 537 ballistic missiles intercepted). MOU signed 17 Jun (Versailles/Tehran; press now styles it the ‘Islamabad Memorandum’ after Pakistan’s mediation): 14 points, 60-day toll-free Hormuz, $300bn reconstruction. Peak of 70 crossings 24 Jun, then the Ever Lovely strike and the 25-27 Jun exchange. 4-6 Jul: Ali Khamenei’s state funeral — crowds openly called for Trump’s death. 7 Jul: Al Rekayat (Qatari LNG) and Wedyan (Saudi VLCC) struck, a third vessel within 24h; US hit ~90 targets and re-imposed oil sanctions. 8-9 Jul: two more strike nights (14 killed, 78 wounded); Iran’s army and IRGC hit Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar and Jordan; Trump declared the ceasefire ‘over.’ 10 Jul: southern-lane traffic collapsed to zero AIS intent. 11 Jul: IRGC hit the GFS Galaxy, declared the strait CLOSED ‘until further notice’; US round-3 strikes answered; Trump and Mojtaba traded personal threats; and the Muscat channel opened — Oman’s two-corridor draft on the table, the most senior US team of the war expected. Day 135: the strait is formally closed, and the deal’s fate compresses into Article 5.
